title: Rust Breach and Clear: raid cost, upkeep, and route check
description: What Breach and Clear changes around a raid: group-scaled TC upkeep, monument blockers, grenade stacks, and the standard explosive math that was separately rechecked.
question: Did Rust Breach and Clear change raid costs or raid preparation?
shortAnswer: The official Breach and Clear notes do not list a direct change to the standard door and wall counts or explosive recipes monitored by RaidBench, and those values passed a separate source check. Preparation still changes: larger authorized groups can add TC upkeep tax, red-keycard monument blockers can delay access, and standardized grenade stack sizes can change inventory planning.
impact: The six monitored vanilla door and wall targets, sulfur-per-item values, and official explosive recipe markers passed a separate post-update verification.
The first four counted players add no new tax; the next six add 2% each, subsequent players add 4% each, and the official maximum tax is 300%.
New blockers appear at monuments with red-keycard puzzle rooms. The official update describes them as damage-gated obstacles and says they begin decaying after 24 hours if not destroyed.
Grenade stack sizes were reduced and standardized, so plans that depend on old carry layouts deserve an in-game inventory check.
Unlocked garage doors can now be picked up without building privilege, matching other doors; teams should recheck assumptions around unsecured access and ownership.
checklist: Use current RaidBench explosive counts only for the six named vanilla targets and methods.
Read the TC's displayed upkeep after the current authorization and code-lock group is established.
Do not assume a red-keycard route is immediately open at the start of a wipe.
Recheck grenade stack sizes in the live inventory before assigning carry roles.
Treat monument blockers, hidden base layers, splash, misses, counters, and custom-server settings as separate route risks.
notChanged: Breach and Clear is not evidence that every old explosive count changed. The post-update verifier found no mismatch in the six monitored target counts, sulfur values, or official recipe markers. It also does not establish a universal cost for the new monument blockers.
refreshTrigger: Review after any Facepunch change to building health, explosive recipes, grenade inventory, group upkeep scaling, or monument blockers.

title: Rust Power Trip raid meta: what changed for compounds and farming
description: The Power Trip changes that affect raid preparation: static high-wall upkeep, tighter water-well stock, safe-zone resource spawns, and powered monument recyclers.
question: Did Rust Power Trip change raid costs or raid preparation?
shortAnswer: The official Power Trip notes do not list a direct recipe or target-count change for rockets, C4, satchels, or explosive ammo. Raid preparation still changes around them: high walls now use a static 20% upkeep cost, water-well vendor stock is tighter, ore nodes and woodpiles no longer spawn in safe zones, and powered monuments can change recycler routing.
impact: No direct explosive recipe or target-count change was found in the official Power Trip notes; RaidBench counts were separately rechecked against the monitored sources.
High walls now have a static upkeep cost of 20%, so large external-TC and wall networks deserve a fresh upkeep calculation.
Stock was reduced from 10 to 2 and restock time increased from 2 minutes to 10 minutes.
Ore nodes and woodpiles can no longer spawn in safe zones.
Power Plant progression can improve recycler operation and unlock a special high-efficiency recycler, changing where teams may choose to process components.
checklist: Keep current explosive counts only after checking the server is vanilla and the RaidBench verification date is current.
Recalculate upkeep for compounds that depend heavily on high walls and external cupboards.
Do not plan a farming route around safe-zone ore nodes or woodpiles.
Treat water-well tools and tea materials as a limited boost rather than a dependable bulk supply.
Recheck recycler risk and travel time before changing the team's component route.
notChanged: Power Trip is not evidence that every old raid guide is invalid. The official notes do not announce direct changes to standard explosive recipes or building target counts; custom servers can still differ.
refreshTrigger: Review after any Facepunch change to explosives, building health, high-wall upkeep, recycler efficiency, vendor stock, or resource spawning.

title: Rust Common Ground raid windows: the Softcore rules that matter
description: A player-focused explanation of Softcore raid windows, Tool Cupboard protection, young-TC exceptions, and what remains attackable.
question: How do Rust raid windows work after the Common Ground update?
shortAnswer: On Softcore servers using the default settings, building blocks and doors inside an eligible Tool Cupboard radius are protected outside the configured raid window. The official default window is 6 PM to 9 PM in the server's local time. A Tool Cupboard must be at least one hour old to provide that protection, and exposed deployables or an unprotected TC can still be attacked.
impact: Softcore players and server owners using the raid-window system.
6 PM to 9 PM in the server's local time; server owners can change it.
Building blocks, doors, floors, roofs, and ladder hatches within an eligible TC radius.
Deployables and a Tool Cupboard that is left exposed.
A Tool Cupboard younger than one hour does not activate raid blocking.
checklist: Confirm the server is running Softcore and has raid windows enabled.
Check the server's local time instead of assuming your own time zone.
Do not rely on a newly placed Tool Cupboard for immediate protection.
Protect deployables and the Tool Cupboard even outside the raid window.
Recheck custom server rules before planning a raid or logging off.
notChanged: The update does not make every object invulnerable outside the window, and custom servers can change the default schedule and related settings.
refreshTrigger: Review when Facepunch changes Softcore raid-window rules, Tool Cupboard protection, or related server variables.

title: Rust Apartment Complex renter checklist
description: What to verify before renting an Apartment Complex room, from included utilities to scrap payments and eviction risk.
question: Is renting an Apartment Complex room worth it in Rust?
shortAnswer: An apartment can accelerate the start of a wipe because room tiers may include storage, furnaces, or other conveniences. Treat the room as rented infrastructure rather than permanent ownership: keep scrap in the slot by the door, confirm what the chosen room includes, and avoid storing everything there until you understand the eviction rules.
impact: Fast early-wipe shelter and utilities while a permanent base is still being planned.
Scrap must be kept in the payment slot next to the room door.
Missed rent can lead to eviction and loss of possessions stored in the room.
Different room tiers offer different space and included conveniences.
Compare rent and location against the time saved on shelter, storage, and smelting.
checklist: Inspect the room tier and included features before paying.
Set aside enough scrap for the full play session and expected offline period.
Keep high-value items in a fallback location until the rent loop is familiar.
Check travel distance to monuments, farming routes, and your planned permanent base.
Move critical loot before the rent buffer reaches zero.
notChanged: An apartment is a temporary logistics option. It does not replace scouting, secure storage discipline, or a permanent base plan.
refreshTrigger: Review if Facepunch changes apartment pricing, room features, eviction behavior, or monument access.

It also fixed a burning status that could continue after touching a campfire. Update the game before resuming important progression, then verify that the expected world and character save loads correctly before making major changes.

Burning status continuing after contact with a campfire.
Install v1.0.1 and verify the correct save before a long session.
Confirm host and client versions match before multiplayer progression.
Keep normal backups where the platform or server workflow allows them.
checklist: Confirm the title screen or platform update history shows v1.0.1 or later.
Load the intended world and check recent structures, inventory, and progression.
Avoid overwriting a suspicious save until the correct file or backup is identified.
For multiplayer, confirm the host has updated before reconnecting.

title: Palworld 1.0 progression reset: Sunreach, Awakening, and Mutation priorities
description: A clean planning order for returning players facing Sunreach, 72 new Pals, Awakening, Mutation, and broad balance changes.
question: What should a returning player do first in Palworld 1.0?
shortAnswer: Start with an audit, not a spending spree. Palworld 1.0 adds Sunreach, 72 new Pals, Awakening and Mutation systems, rebalanced Pals, and large changes to base building and multiplayer. Verify the old base loop, rebuild one dependable production chain, review the combat team under the new balance, and only then commit rare materials to the new strengthening systems.
impact: Sunreach expands exploration and progression routes.
72 new Pals raise the total to 287 in the official release notes.
Awakening and Mutation add new strengthening decisions.
Pal stats and abilities were broadly rebalanced.
Base building, multiplayer, and other systems received large overhauls.
checklist: Load the existing base and identify broken or slower production links.
Recheck work suitability and combat roles after the broad Pal rebalance.
Establish one stable food, sphere, repair, and transport loop.
Scout Sunreach with recovery supplies and spare capture resources.
Test Awakening and Mutation on a controlled target before using scarce materials widely.
notChanged: A major release does not make every older strategy useless. Keep any loop that still produces the required materials safely and consistently.

source.label: Palworld Steam announcement - v1.0 Official Release Changelog

refreshTrigger: Review after Palworld balance patches, Awakening or Mutation changes, or Sunreach progression updates.

title: POE2 0.4.0i build impact check
description: Which builds and boss situations are directly affected by the official 0.4.0i fixes, and which guides do not need a broad rewrite.
question: Does POE2 patch 0.4.0i make my build guide outdated?
shortAnswer: Patch 0.4.0i is a narrow fix set, not a broad balance pass. Recheck a guide if it depends on critical-hit chance after shapeshifting or if it discussed bosses failing to emerge with a stolen Proximal Intangibility modifier. Builds outside those cases do not become outdated solely because of this patch, although older patch and economy checks still apply.
impact: A shapeshifting critical-hit condition was fixed so it no longer depends on another shapeshift-tracking stat.
Some bosses failing to emerge with a stolen Proximal Intangibility modifier were fixed.
The patch added support for upcoming race events.
A Phoenix level-up effect trigger was corrected.
No broad skill, passive, item, or economy rebalance is listed in 0.4.0i.
checklist: Check whether the build uses shapeshifting and the named critical-hit condition.
Remove any workaround that only existed for the fixed tracking bug.
Re-test the affected damage condition in a controlled encounter.
Do not label unrelated builds outdated from this patch alone.
Continue checking the guide's original patch, required items, and economy assumptions.
notChanged: The patch notes do not announce a general build rebalance, so unrelated skill trees and item priorities require their own evidence before being changed.

title: POE2 Wolf Pack Spirit bug: official hotfix status and cleanup steps
description: The official status of the Wolf Pack Spirit reservation bug and a short checklist for removing old workaround advice.
question: Is the POE2 Wolf Pack permanent Spirit reservation bug still active?
shortAnswer: Grinding Gear Games states that 0.4.0h Hotfix 1 fixed Wolf Pack permanently reserving Spirit until the skill gem was removed. Guides that tell players to repeatedly remove the gem as the primary workaround are now stale for updated clients. Install the current game version, rebuild the weapon-swap state once, and investigate separately if the reservation problem continues.
impact: Wolf Pack could permanently reserve Spirit until its gem was removed.
Pre-hotfix workaround instructions should be labeled historical or removed.
Update, re-equip the setup, and retest weapon swapping.
Record the current version and setup, then treat it as a separate unresolved case.
checklist: Install 0.4.0h Hotfix 1 or any later client version.
Remove and reinsert the Wolf Pack gem once to clear an old state.
Test both weapon sets and record the Spirit total before and after swapping.
Discard guides that present the pre-hotfix workaround as current behavior.
If the issue remains, capture the exact setup and report it against the current version.
notChanged: The hotfix addresses the named permanent reservation bug; it does not prove that every Spirit, companion, or weapon-swap issue has the same cause.
